title: When the Tide Burns
premise: Jonah Reyes, a widowed single father running Port Merrow's only bookshop, has spent three years rebuilding his life in careful, small steps — until the town library's anonymous pen-pal program accidentally pairs him with ADA Vivian Cross, the prosecutor who once tried to shutter his late wife's family business and whom he has publicly despised ever since. Their letters, written without knowing identities, crack both of them open even as their daytime selves wage war over a corruption case Vivian is building against the developer syndicate quietly buying the waterfront — a syndicate Jonah's brother-in-law works for, and one that has begun threatening the bookshop itself. When their identities are exposed mid-crisis, betrayal nearly destroys what the letters built, but Vivian's case collapses under witness intimidation, forcing her to choose between the law that failed her and the justice she can pursue only by trusting Jonah and the town she once looked down on. In the end, they take the syndicate down together outside the courtroom, and Jonah finally risks the whole heart, choosing love against every instinct for safety as the tide of his carefully guarded life burns clean through.
about_author: Gideon Delacroix is the pen name of a former small-town bookseller who spent a decade watching love stories walk through the door before deciding to write them. Known for slow-burn romances laced with moral reckoning, Delacroix writes from a coastal cottage with a rescue dog and an unreasonable number of unread paperbacks.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Steps
chapters.summary: Jonah POV. Three years after his wife's death, Jonah runs the bookshop and raises his daughter Marisol in careful, measured routines. A developer's surveyor measures the storefront, an omen he dismisses. Emotional beat: the fragile peace of a life built to avoid falling again.

chapters.title: The Prosecutor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Vivian POV. ADA Vivian Cross returns to Port Merrow to build a corruption case against the Halvard Group, whose shell companies are devouring the waterfront. Her ambition is armor over a past failure. Emotional beat: cold competence hiding a hunger to matter.

chapters.title: Enemies in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Jonah POV. Vivian enters the bookshop researching property records; they clash publicly over her old case against his late wife's family café. Marisol witnesses the fight, embarrassed. Emotional beat: old wounds reopened, mutual contempt freshly sharpened.

chapters.title: An Anonymous Kindness
chapters.summary: Vivian POV. The library's pen-pal program, meant to connect isolated townsfolk, suffers a clerical error — the coordinator, flustered by their public feud, assigns Jonah and Vivian to each other, names withheld. Emotional beat: irony set in motion; the reader knows, they don't.

chapters.title: First Letter
chapters.summary: Jonah POV. Jonah writes his first anonymous letter as an act of grief therapy his therapist suggested, confessing he's forgotten how to want things. His correspondent's reply is sharp, funny, unexpectedly honest. Emotional beat: cautious curiosity.

chapters.title: The Case Against the Waterfront
chapters.summary: Vivian POV. Vivian interviews a frightened dockworker who hints at falsified environmental reports. Her subpoena is quashed by a friendly judge. Emotional beat: the first taste of a wall she can't argue down.

chapters.title: Letters and Loathing
chapters.summary: Jonah POV. Daytime: Jonah refuses Vivian's request to post notices for displaced tenants. Night: their letters deepen — she admits she fears she's becoming what she prosecutes. Emotional beat: dramatic irony tightening; each likes the stranger, loathes the neighbor.

chapters.title: Marisol's Map
chapters.summary: Marisol POV (young voice). Marisol draws a map of the town marking places she loves — the pier, the shop, the lighthouse steps — for a school project on 'what's worth saving.' Emotional beat: innocence that quietly names the stakes.

chapters.title: The Quashed Subpoena
chapters.summary: Vivian POV. Vivian's star witness recants after a 'friendly visit' from Halvard security. Her supervisor suggests she settle for a minor charge. Emotional beat: the law's machinery grinding against her ideals.

chapters.title: Confessions on Paper
chapters.summary: Jonah POV. Jonah confesses in a letter that he once hated someone so completely it frightened him. The reply: 'Hate is just love with the wrong address.' He reads it five times. Emotional beat: a crack of light through the armor.

chapters.title: Coffee, Unknowing
chapters.summary: Vivian POV. Vivian and Jonah, forced to co-organize the harbor fundraiser, work late and almost enjoy it — then sabotage the moment with an argument over the syndicate. Emotional beat: attraction flickering under hostility.

chapters.title: The Brother-in-Law
chapters.summary: Jonah POV. Jonah's brother-in-law Theo, who works for Halvard, warns him the bookshop's lease is targeted and offers a buyout. Jonah refuses. Emotional beat: family loyalty curdling into threat.

chapters.title: What the Letters Know
chapters.summary: Vivian POV. Vivian realizes her pen-pal is a local, and that she's telling him things she's told no one — including doubts about the case. She almost quits the program. She doesn't. Emotional beat: addiction to honesty.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Jonah POV. Halvard's men vandalize the shop's window; insurance balks. Marisol has nightmares. Jonah writes to his pen-pal about fear for the first time. Emotional beat: safety eroding, the small-steps life cracking.

chapters.title: The Fundraiser
chapters.summary: Vivian POV. At the harbor fundraiser, Vivian publicly confronts a Halvard executive with evidence Jonah unknowingly helped her find — a ledger page from the bookshop's used-book donation bin. Emotional beat: their two worlds colliding through coincidence.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Jonah POV. After the fundraiser, adrenaline and rain; Jonah and Vivian nearly kiss on the lighthouse steps, then retreat, each ashamed of wanting the enemy. Emotional beat: longing denied, desire acknowledged.

chapters.title: The Letter That Gives It Away
chapters.summary: Vivian POV. Jonah mentions Marisol's lighthouse map in a letter; Vivian, who saw the map at the fundraiser, freezes. She now knows. Emotional beat: knowledge as a burden — she says nothing.

chapters.title: Theo's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Jonah POV. Theo reveals Halvard knows about Vivian's investigation and pressures Jonah to hand over the ledger page 'for family.' Jonah refuses; Theo implies Marisol's school route passes the docks. Emotional beat: menace wearing a family face.

chapters.title: Crossing the Line
chapters.summary: Vivian POV. Vivian's witness is hospitalized in a 'car accident.' Out of legal options, she photographs sealed evidence to build a parallel case — her first step outside the law. Emotional beat: the fall from procedural grace.

chapters.title: The Whole Heart
chapters.summary: Jonah POV. Jonah writes his pen-pal that he's ready to risk the whole heart instead of lending pieces — and that he thinks he's falling for someone impossible in daylight. Emotional beat: courage on paper, cowardice in person.

chapters.title: Midpoint: Two Truths
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Jonah and Vivian, working late on the tenant-defense files, share a real, tender conversation — the closest they've come. Both leave aching, each comparing the living person to the letter-writer and finding the stranger winning. Emotional beat: love arriving by two doors.

chapters.title: The Kiss
chapters.summary: Vivian POV. After she wins a temporary injunction saving the bookshop block, they kiss in the empty shop among the paperbacks. It is real, and it is a mistake, and neither pulls away. Emotional beat: surrender.

chapters.title: Happiness as a Target
chapters.summary: Jonah POV. One week of stolen mornings and Marisol's cautious approval — until Theo photographs them together and delivers the photos to Halvard. Emotional beat: joy painted on a target.

chapters.title: The Exposure
chapters.summary: Vivian POV. Halvard leaks the pen-pal correspondence to the press: 'Prosecutor's Secret Lover Fed Her Evidence.' The letters — their most private truths — become headlines. Emotional beat: intimacy weaponized.

chapters.title: Betrayal in Broad Daylight
chapters.summary: Jonah POV. Jonah learns Vivian knew his identity from the lighthouse map and said nothing. Feeling used — a source, not a partner — he ends it and burns her letters in the shop's back room, then can't finish the last one. Emotional beat: the heart's whole risk punished.

chapters.title: Suspension
chapters.summary: Vivian POV. Vivian is suspended pending ethics review; her case is reassigned to a prosecutor who settles with Halvard within days. The tenants' injunction will lapse. Emotional beat: the law she served discarding her.

chapters.title: Marisol's Question
chapters.summary: Marisol POV. Marisol asks Jonah why being scared of loving someone is a reason to stop. Her lighthouse map hangs crooked on the shop wall. Emotional beat: a child's clarity cutting through adult ruin.

chapters.title: The Last Letter
chapters.summary: Vivian POV. Vivian writes one final letter she doesn't send, telling the truth about when she knew, why she stayed silent, and what the letters meant. She leaves it in a used copy of her favorite novel on Jonah's shelf. Emotional beat: humility as a doorway.

chapters.title: Reading by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Jonah POV. Jonah finds the book while re-shelving — her handwriting. He reads the unsent letter three times, then walks to her apartment in the rain and stands there without knocking. Emotional beat: pride versus forgiveness, forgiveness winning by inches.

chapters.title: Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Both POV, alternating. Vivian lays out what she can't do in court and what they can do outside it: the ledger page, the dockworkers' testimony, Theo's conscience, and the press. Jonah must decide whether to weaponize the shop he built for safety. Emotional beat: alliance reborn as partnership.

chapters.title: Theo's Choice
chapters.summary: Jonah POV. Jonah confronts Theo with evidence of Halvard falsifying the accident report. Theo, terrified but finally ashamed, agrees to testify — off the record, outside the law. Emotional beat: a family fracture becoming a family's redemption.

chapters.title: The Dockworkers' Night
chapters.summary: Vivian POV. Vivian and Jonah secretly gather the intimidated witnesses in the bookshop after hours, among the shelves, to record testimony Halvard can't intimidate out of existence. Emotional beat: a bookshop becoming a sanctuary of justice.

chapters.title: Halvard Strikes
chapters.summary: Jonah POV. Halvard files to seize the shop's block immediately and sends men to clear it early — with Marisol inside for story hour. Jonah stands in the doorway and refuses to move. Emotional beat: the small-steps life ends; he plants himself like a tide wall.

chapters.title: Climax: The Tide Burns
chapters.summary: Both POV. At the emergency council meeting, Vivian presents the recorded testimony and Theo's affidavit while the dockworkers stand and speak; the press runs it live; the council voids the seizure and refers Halvard to federal prosecutors. Jonah, called to speak, declares the shop — and his heart — not for sale. Emotional beat: justice outside the law vindicated in public.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Fire
chapters.summary: Vivian POV. Vivian, cleared by the ethics board for her whistleblowing rather than punished, declines reinstatement — she'll practice tenant law from an office above the bookshop. Emotional beat: power renounced, purpose reclaimed.

chapters.title: What Marisol Knew
chapters.summary: Marisol POV. Marisol reveals she'd figured out the pen-pal secret weeks ago and slipped Vivian's novel onto the shelf herself. She asks Vivian, formally, if she's staying. Emotional beat: the child who named the stakes now blesses the ending.

chapters.title: The Reply
chapters.summary: Jonah POV. Jonah writes one last pen-pal letter — signed this time — and reads it aloud to Vivian in the shop after closing: an apology, a confession, a proposal to keep writing to each other forever, in person. Emotional beat: the whole heart, finally risked.

chapters.title: Epilogue: New Shelves
chapters.summary: Vivian POV. Spring. The shop reopens with a tenant-rights lending shelf and a reading nook Marisol designed; Theo stocks the maritime section as penance and peace. Emotional beat: a life rebuilt in larger, braver steps.

chapters.title: The Tide Comes In
chapters.summary: Jonah POV, final chapter. On the lighthouse steps where they once almost kissed, Jonah and Vivian watch the tide come in over a waterfront that will stay the town's. He is no longer a man measured in small safe steps. Emotional beat: love against duty, resolved — the heart and the town, both kept.

chapters.title: Author's Note: Letters Worth Writing
chapters.summary: Author's voice. Delacroix reflects on the real coastal towns losing their waterfronts, the anonymous-kindness programs that inspired the novel, and a closing invitation: write the letter you're afraid to send. Emotional beat: the story handed to the reader like a book across a counter.
